He, may He be exalted, informs about what He has prepared for the disbelievers among His creation: chains, shackles and the blaze, which is the flame and the burning fire in the Hellfire, as He said: ﴿When the shackles are around their necks, and the chains; they will be dragged through scalding water, then in the Fire they will be burned.﴾ [Ghafir: 71, 72].

When He had mentioned what He had prepared for these wretched people of the blazing Fire, He said after it: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor.﴾ The effect of camphor in cooling and its pleasant fragrance is well known, in addition to the delight that accompanies it in Paradise.

Al-Hasan said: "The coolness of the camphor is combined with the fragrance of ginger." Therefore He said: ﴿a spring from which the servants of Allah drink, making it gush forth in abundance.﴾ That is: this which is mixed for these righteous people of camphor is a spring from which those brought near among the servants of Allah drink purely, without mixture, and are satisfied by it. Therefore the verb yashrabu (drink) has been given the sense of yarwā (be quenched/satisfied), so that it takes the preposition bi- (with), and ﴿ʿaynan﴾ (a spring) is in the accusative as a specification (tamyīz).

Some of them said: "This drink, in its pleasantness, is like camphor." Others said: "It is from a spring of camphor." And others said: "It is permissible that it be in the accusative by ﴿yashrabu﴾." Ibn Jarir related these three opinions.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿they make it gush forth in abundance﴾, that is: they dispose of it wherever they wish and however they wish, from their palaces, their homes, their assemblies and their dwelling places.

Tafjīr (causing to gush forth) means inbāʿ (making to flow), as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth"﴾ [al-Isra: 90]. And He said: ﴿And We caused a river to gush forth between them﴾ [al-Kahf: 33].

Mujahid said: ﴿they make it gush forth in abundance﴾ means "they lead it wherever they wish." Likewise said ʿIkrima and Qatada. Al-Thawri said: "They turn it wherever they wish."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿They fulfil their vows and fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾, that is: they worship Allah by fulfilling what He has made obligatory upon them of the obligatory acts of obedience by the basic law, and what they have made obligatory upon themselves by way of vow (nadhr).

Imam Malik said, from Talha ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Aylī, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from ʿAʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever vows to obey Allah, let him obey Him; and whoever vows to disobey Allah, let him not disobey Him." Al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Malik.

And they abstain from the prohibited acts which He forbade them, out of fear of the evil reckoning on the Day of Return, which is the Day whose evil is widespread, that is: spreading and general upon the people, except for those whom Allah has mercy upon.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Spreading out." Qatada said: "By Allah, the evil of that Day will spread until it fills the heavens and the earth."

Ibn Jarir said: From this is their saying: istaṭāra al-ṣadʿ fī al-zujāja wa-istaṭāl (the crack spread in the glass and extended). From this is the saying of al-Aʿsha:

"She departed, having left in the heart a crack, spreading despite her distance."

That is: extending and spreading.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it﴾, it has been said: "Despite their love for Allah, the Exalted." They took the pronoun as referring to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because the context indicates it. But the more apparent view is that the pronoun refers to the food, that is: they give food while they love it and desire it. This was said by Mujahid and Muqatil, and Ibn Jarir preferred it, like His saying: ﴿and gives wealth despite love for it﴾ [al-Baqara: 177], and like His saying: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love﴾ [Al ʿImran: 92].

Al-Bayhaqi narrated, by way of al-Aʿmash, from Nafiʿ who said: Ibn ʿUmar fell ill and craved grapes, at the first arrival of grapes. So Safiyya, that is his wife, sent someone and bought a bunch for a dirham. A beggar followed the messenger, and when he entered with it, the beggar said: "The beggar!" Ibn ʿUmar said: "Give it to him." So they gave it to him. Then she sent another dirham and bought a bunch, and the beggar followed the messenger again, and when he entered, the beggar said: "The beggar!" Ibn ʿUmar said: "Give it to him." So they gave it to him. Then Safiyya sent to the beggar and said: "By Allah, if you return, you will never obtain any good from him again." Then she sent another dirham and bought with it...

And in the Sahih: "The best charity is that you give while you are healthy and miserly, hoping for wealth and fearing poverty." That is: in a state of your love for wealth, your greed for it and your need of it. Therefore He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan and the captive﴾. As for the needy and the orphan, their explanation and description has already preceded. As for the captive: Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said: "The captive is from the People of the Qibla (Muslims)." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Their captives on that day were polytheists." What supports this is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded his companions on the Day of Badr to honour the captives, so they would give them precedence over themselves at the meal. Likewise said Saʿid ibn Jubayr, ʿAṭāʾ, al-Hasan and Qatada.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) enjoined kindness to slaves in more than one hadith, to the extent that among the last things he enjoined was that he kept saying: "Prayer, and what your right hands possess." Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad from the hadith of ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him.

ʿIkrima said: "They are the slaves," and Ibn Jarir preferred this, because the verse is general for the Muslim and the polytheist.

Mujahid said: "It is the prisoner." That is: they give food to these while they crave it and love it, saying with the tongue of their state: ﴿We feed you only for the countenance of Allah﴾, that is: seeking the reward and pleasure of Allah, ﴿we do not want from you any reward or thanks﴾, that is: we do not seek from you a recompense which you repay us with, nor that you thank us among the people.

Mujahid and Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: "Indeed, by Allah, they did not say it with their tongues, but Allah knew it from their hearts, so He praised them for it, so that whoever desires it may be eager for it."

﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day, frowning and distressing﴾, that is: we only do this, hoping that Allah will have mercy on us and receive us with His kindness, on the frowning, distressing Day.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talha said, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿ʿabūsan﴾ (frowning) means narrow; ﴿qamṭarīran﴾ (distressing) means long.

ʿIkrima and others said, from him, regarding His saying: ﴿a Day, frowning, distressing﴾: the disbeliever frowns on that Day until sweat like tar flows from between his eyes.

Mujahid said: ﴿ʿabūsan﴾: one whose lips are contracted; ﴿qamṭarīran﴾: he said: the contracting of the face with scowling.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Qatada said: faces frown in it from the terror, and ﴿qamṭarīran﴾ is the contracting of the forehead and what is between the eyes from the terror.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 76, verses 23–31:

Allah the Exalted says, bestowing favour upon His Messenger ﷺ through what He sent down to him of the Mighty Qur'an, a sending down: ﴿So be patient for the decree of your Lord﴾, meaning: just as I have honoured you with what I have sent down to you, so be patient with His decree and His measure, and know that He will manage your affairs with His good management. ﴿And do not obey from among them any sinner or ungrateful one﴾, meaning: do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites if they want to turn you away from what has been sent down to you [[In A: "to you".]], but rather convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and put your trust in Allah, for Allah will protect you from the people. The sinner (ātim) is the one who is wicked in his deeds, and the ungrateful (kafūr) is the one who disbelieves in his heart.

﴿And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening﴾, meaning: at the beginning of the day and at its end.

﴿And during the night, prostrate to Him and glorify Him through the long night﴾, like His saying: ﴿And from the night, pray tahajjud with it as a supererogatory act for you; it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ [al-Isra' 79], and like His saying: ﴿O you who wrap yourself in garments, stand [in prayer] at night, except a little, half of it, or subtract from it a little, or add to it, and recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾ [al-Muzzammil 1–4].

Then He said, denouncing the disbelievers and those who resemble them in their love of this world, their attraction to it, their absorption in it, and their turning their backs on the Hereafter: ﴿Indeed, these love the immediate [life] and leave behind them a heavy Day﴾, meaning: the Day of Resurrection.

Then He said: ﴿We created them and strengthened their joints﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said: meaning, their creation. ﴿And if We wish, We can replace their likes with a complete replacement﴾, meaning: and if We wish, We will resurrect them on the Day of Resurrection and replace them, recreating them as a new creation. This is an argument from the first creation to the return.

Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jarir said: ﴿And if We wish, We can replace their likes with a complete replacement﴾ [meaning]: and if We wish, We will bring a different people other than them, like His saying: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others; and Allah is ever capable of that﴾ [al-Nisa' 133], and like His saying: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you and bring a new creation. And that is not difficult for Allah﴾ [Ibrahim 19–20; Fatir 16–17].

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, this﴾, meaning: this Surah, ﴿is a reminder, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way﴾, meaning: a path and a course. That is, whoever wills, let him be guided by the Qur'an, like His saying: ﴿And what would it harm them if they had believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent from what Allah has provided them? And ever is Allah Knowing of them﴾ [al-Nisa' 39].

Then He said: ﴿And you will not, except that Allah wills﴾, meaning: no one can guide himself, nor enter into faith, nor bring benefit to himself, ﴿except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾, meaning: He knows who deserves guidance and facilitates it for him and provides its means, and who deserves misguidance and turns him away from guidance. To Him belongs perfect wisdom and conclusive proof. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾.

Then He said: ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy; but the wrongdoers – He has prepared for them a painful punishment﴾, meaning: He guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills. Whomever He guides, none can misguide, and whomever He misguides, none can guide.

[End of Surah al-Insan] [Addition from M, A.] [And Allah knows best] [Addition from A.]
